prompt: Of the checks on the lesson's ladder, which is the only one that costs money on a real account?
hint: Which one creates something?

choices.text: `terraform validate`
choices.why: It reads files and the providers' schemas; it never calls an API.

choices.text: A test run with `command = plan`
choices.why: A plan asks AWS questions and creates nothing.

choices.text: `terraform fmt -check`
choices.why: It looks at the layout of files and needs nothing at all.

choices.text: A test run with `command = apply`
choices.why: Yes. It builds the resources, and on a real account they are billed while they exist.

prompt: What does `terraform validate` need before it can check a configuration?
hint: The schema it checks against lives somewhere.

choices.text: Credentials that the account accepts
choices.why: It makes no API call, so it needs none.

choices.text: The providers installed
choices.why: Right. The schemas are inside the providers, which is why a fresh checkout needs `terraform init` first.

choices.text: A value for each variable that has no default
choices.why: It printed `Success!` for a module with three such variables and no values.

choices.text: A state file from an earlier apply
choices.why: It never reads the state; the module in the lesson had never been applied.

prompt: Match each check with what it can find.
hint: Each rung finds what the one above it cannot.

pairs.right: An argument the provider does not have
A subnet named differently from the test's expectation
A range AWS refuses to create

right_distractors: A change somebody made by hand last week

prompt: Put the checks in the order of the lesson's ladder, cheapest first.
hint: From layout to a real apply.
trap: `validate` comes after `fmt` because it needs the providers installed, and `fmt` needs nothing.

prompt: What exit status did `terraform fmt -check -diff` return when `outputs.tf` was out of layout?
hint: The capture printed it after the diff.

prompt: The module has three variables and none has a default. Why did `terraform validate` print `Success!` without asking for any value?
hint: What does it check, and what does it never look at?

choices.text: It filled each one with an empty string
choices.why: It does not invent values; it never evaluates the variables at all.

choices.text: It read them from `terraform.tfvars`
choices.why: There is no such file in the module, and `validate` would not read it anyway.

choices.text: It checks the configuration, not the values
choices.why: Yes. That is its strength and its limit: no value means no question about a value.

choices.text: A module's variables are only checked by the root module that calls it
choices.why: The module was validated on its own, and the variables were still never asked for.

prompt: In a fresh checkout, `terraform validate` stops with `Missing required provider`. Which command should a pipeline run first, without touching the state?
hint: It installs what the configuration needs.

choices.text: `terraform providers lock`
choices.why: That records checksums in the lock file; it installs nothing into the working directory.

choices.text: `terraform plan -refresh=false`
choices.why: A plan needs the providers too, and it would also need the backend and values.

choices.text: `terraform init -backend=false`
choices.why: Right: providers and modules are installed and the state is left alone.

choices.text: `terraform fmt -recursive`
choices.why: That rewrites layout and installs nothing.

prompt: Run as `terraform fmt ___`, the command rewrites nothing and exits with a non-zero status when a file is out of layout.
hint: A flag of one word.

prompt: Which files does `terraform test` read?
hint: Written in HCL, under `tests/` by default.

choices.text: `*_test.tf`
choices.why: A `.tf` file would be part of the configuration itself.

choices.text: `*.tfvars`
choices.why: Those hold values, not tests.

choices.text: `*.tftest.hcl`
choices.why: Yes, in the module's directory and in `tests/`.

choices.text: `*_test.go`
choices.why: That is a Go test, which is how Terratest is written, not `terraform test`.

prompt: The module has no `provider` block, but `plan.tftest.hcl` has one. Why?
hint: Who configures providers for a module?

choices.text: In a test, the file is the module's caller
choices.why: Right. A module leaves provider configuration to whoever calls it, and here that is the test file.

choices.text: `terraform test` overrides the module's provider block with the one in the test file
choices.why: The module has no provider block to override.

choices.text: To switch off the credentials check
choices.why: The block only sets the region; the credentials were still checked, as the dead-endpoint run showed.

choices.text: Without it, the plan would run against the real AWS instead of moto
choices.why: `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL` sends calls to moto either way.

prompt: With `command = plan`, the assertion `aws_subnet.this["a"].vpc_id == aws_vpc.this.id` failed with `Unknown condition value`. Why?
hint: Who invents a VPC's id, and when?

choices.text: `vpc_id` is not an attribute an assertion may read
choices.why: It is; the end-to-end run asserted on it after an apply.

choices.text: Both ids exist only after AWS creates the resources
choices.why: Yes. During a plan they are unknown, and Terraform refuses to call an unknown condition a pass.

choices.text: The subnet had been placed in the default VPC
choices.why: Nothing was placed anywhere; a plan creates nothing.

choices.text: moto had stopped answering
choices.why: The run reached the assertion, so the provider had been configured.

prompt: Inside a `run` block, `command = ___` makes the run create nothing, and its assertions are checked against what Terraform would do.
hint: The other value is `apply`.

prompt: With `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL` pointing at a port where nothing listens, both runs of `plan.tftest.hcl` reported `skip` rather than `fail`. Why?
hint: Read the error under the two runs.

choices.text: A plan run is never allowed to fail
choices.why: The same file failed earlier, when the subnet names changed.

choices.text: Terraform skips plan runs when the state is empty
choices.why: The state was empty on every run of this lesson, and they ran.

choices.text: The provider could not be configured, so no run was attempted
choices.why: Right: the credentials check against STS found nothing listening.

choices.text: Their assertions had no values to compare
choices.why: The variables were set; the runs never got as far as the assertions.

prompt: Under `mock_provider "aws" {}` alone, the precondition reported that `sa-east-1a` is not a zone the region offers. Why?
hint: What did the error say the list of names was?

choices.text: The mock answers in `us-east-1` unless told otherwise
choices.why: The mock invents strings; it has no region of its own to answer from.

choices.text: The mock returned an empty list of zones
choices.why: Yes. A mock answers a list with an empty one, so no zone existed until the override supplied some.

choices.text: Preconditions are not evaluated under a mock, so the zone was never checked
choices.why: It was evaluated, which is why it failed.

choices.text: moto has no zone called `sa-east-1a`
choices.why: moto was never asked; the endpoint pointed at nothing.

prompt: Which of these did the mock provider in `unit.tftest.hcl` do? Choose all that apply.
hint: Look at the `-verbose` output and at what was never asked.

choices.text: Invented a value for the subnet's `arn`
choices.why: Yes, eight random characters.

choices.text: Called the AWS API to read the zones
choices.why: It never calls an API; the zones came from Ana's override.

choices.text: Kept the VPC id Ana set with `override_resource`
choices.why: Yes; the subnet's `vpc_id` came out as that value.

choices.text: Refused a subnet range outside the VPC
choices.why: Nothing in a mock knows that rule; AWS enforced it in the end-to-end run.

choices.text: Let the run apply without creating anything
choices.why: Yes; the run had no `command = plan`, so it applied, to the mock.

prompt: Which block gave `data.aws_availability_zones.here` the list of São Paulo zones in the unit test?
hint: It targets one data source by its address.

choices.text: `override_resource`
choices.why: That one fixed the VPC's id; it targets a resource.

choices.text: `expect_failures`
choices.why: That lists objects that must fail; it supplies no values.

choices.text: `variables`
choices.why: The zones are not an input of the module.

choices.text: `override_data`
choices.why: Right, with `target = data.aws_availability_zones.here`.

prompt: In `rules.tftest.hcl`, the run `cidr_without_a_mask` sets `cidr = "10.20.0.0"` and `expect_failures = [var.cidr]`. When does it pass?
hint: The list names an object, not just an outcome.

choices.text: When the plan completes with no error at all
choices.why: Then the rule let a bad value through, and the run fails.

choices.text: When the variable's own rule refuses the value
choices.why: Yes. A refusal from anywhere else does not count, as the loosened rule showed.

choices.text: When the provider refuses the range
choices.why: That happened with the loosened rule, and the run failed with `Missing expected failure`.

choices.text: When the apply against AWS fails
choices.why: The run only plans, against a mock; nothing reaches AWS.

prompt: With the rule loosened to `can(regex("^[0-9./]+$", var.cidr))`, the value `10.20.0.0` was still refused. Why did the run fail anyway?
hint: Who refused it?

choices.text: `expect_failures` cannot be used together with a mock provider
choices.why: The same file passed with the mock before the rule was loosened.

choices.text: The regular expression itself was invalid
choices.why: It was valid, and it matched `10.20.0.0`; that was the problem.

choices.text: The provider refused it, and `var.cidr` did not
choices.why: Right. The failure came from the AWS provider's check on `cidr_block`, not from the object the test named.

choices.text: The zone run that followed it also failed
choices.why: That run was skipped, not failed.

prompt: After `cidr_without_a_mask` failed, `zone_from_another_region` reported `skip`. What does that say about the zone rule?
hint: A skipped run was not attempted.

choices.text: It is broken as well
choices.why: A broken rule would have produced a failure, not a skip.

choices.text: It passed, since a skip is counted as a pass
choices.why: The summary counts skips apart: `0 passed, 1 failed, 1 skipped`.

choices.text: This run says nothing about it
choices.why: Yes. Terraform did not carry on past the failed run, so the zone rule was not tested at all.

choices.text: Its precondition was removed by the failure
choices.why: A test changes no file; the precondition is still in `main.tf`.

prompt: When the object named in `expect_failures` lets a bad value through, Terraform reports the error `Missing expected ___`.
hint: The error is in English in both languages.

prompt: In `range.tftest.hcl`, `plan_accepts_it` passed and `apply_refuses_it` failed for a subnet of `10.30.1.0/24` in a VPC of `10.20.0.0/16`. What refused the subnet?
hint: Read the error code.

choices.text: The zone precondition in `main.tf`
choices.why: The zone was `sa-east-1a`, which the region offers.

choices.text: `terraform validate`, run by the test before the apply
choices.why: The test runs no `validate`, and it would have no values to look at.

choices.text: The API, with `InvalidSubnet.Range`
choices.why: Yes. Only the apply asked AWS to create it, and AWS said no.

choices.text: The validation rule on `subnets`
choices.why: That rule did not exist yet; Ana added it after this run.

prompt: How does the run `aws_agrees` get the VPC id that `build` created?
hint: An earlier run's outputs are addressable.

choices.text: `module.build.vpc_id`
choices.why: `build` is a run, not a module call.

choices.text: `run.build.vpc_id`
choices.why: Right: the output `vpc_id` of the run called `build`.

choices.text: `data.aws_vpc.built.id`
choices.why: That data source needs the id first; it is what reads the VPC back.

choices.text: `output.vpc_id`
choices.why: Inside `aws_agrees` the module under test is the helper, which has no such output.

prompt: After the end-to-end file ran, `describe-vpcs` listed exactly one VPC. Which one?
hint: Its range was `172.31.0.0/16`.

choices.text: The one `build` created, kept for the next run
choices.why: The teardown destroyed it.

choices.text: The default VPC moto creates
choices.why: Yes, as AWS does in every region; the test's own VPC was gone.

choices.text: A VPC created by the helper module
choices.why: The helper only has data sources; it creates nothing.

choices.text: A copy left by a failed teardown
choices.why: The teardown reported success, and the VPC listed is marked as the default.

prompt: Which of these are reasons the lesson gives for running end-to-end tests less often than the rest? Choose all that apply.
hint: Cost, speed and what can be left behind.

choices.text: On a real account they create resources that are billed
choices.why: Yes; the lab used moto, so nothing was billed here.

choices.text: They cannot run against moto
choices.why: The lesson ran them against moto.

choices.text: They are the slowest rung of the ladder
choices.why: Yes, they build and destroy real resources.

choices.text: A failed teardown leaves resources behind
choices.why: Yes, which is what the help text tells you to watch.

choices.text: Assertions are not allowed in a run that applies
choices.why: `build` asserted on the subnets after applying.

prompt: How many runs passed in the final `terraform test` of the whole suite?
hint: Four files: two, two, three and one.

prompt: Put in order what Ana did with the out-of-range subnet, from discovery to a cheap test.
hint: The end-to-end failure came first.
items: An apply in a test fails with `InvalidSubnet.Range`
A validation rule on `subnets` compares each range with the VPC's
A run expecting `var.subnets` to fail joins `rules.tftest.hcl`
The mocked rules pass with no AWS reachable
trap: The test for the rule comes after the rule: before it, `expect_failures = [var.subnets]` would report a missing failure.

prompt: A module's variable `instance_type` has a validation that allows only `t3.` types. Which test checks that rule with no cloud access at all?
hint: No AWS, and a refusal that must come from the variable.

choices.text: An apply run against moto that asserts the type of the instance it created
choices.why: moto is an API; the question asked for no cloud at all, and this tests the accepted case, not the refusal.

choices.text: `terraform validate` with `-var instance_type=m5.large`
choices.why: `validate` never evaluates values, so the rule would not run.

choices.text: A mocked plan with `m5.large` and `expect_failures = [var.instance_type]`
choices.why: Yes: the mock removes AWS, and `expect_failures` demands the refusal from that variable.

choices.text: A plan run against AWS with an `assert` that the type starts with `t3.`
choices.why: It needs AWS, and it checks a good value rather than the rule's refusal.

prompt: A run with `command = plan` asserts that `aws_instance.web.private_ip` starts with `10.20.`. No override sets that address. What happens?
hint: Who chooses the address, and when?

choices.text: It fails with `Unknown condition value`
choices.why: Yes. AWS assigns the address on creation, so during a plan it is unknown, as the subnet's `vpc_id` was.

choices.text: It passes, because the subnet's range starts with `10.20.`
choices.why: Terraform does not infer an address from a range; the value is unknown.

choices.text: It is skipped until an apply provides the value
choices.why: Skips happen when a run is not attempted; this one is attempted and errors.

choices.text: It passes, and the check moves to the apply
choices.why: Terraform refuses to call an unknown condition a pass.

prompt: A colleague proposes deleting the end-to-end file, because the unit tests pass under a mock. Which of these would then go unchecked? Choose all that apply.
hint: Which questions only AWS can answer?

choices.text: A typo in an argument name
choices.why: `validate` catches that, with no AWS.

choices.text: Whether AWS reports the network as the module described it
choices.why: Yes; only `aws_agrees` read it back from AWS.

choices.text: A range AWS refuses for a reason no rule knows yet
choices.why: Yes; that is how the out-of-range subnet was found.

choices.text: A rule that accepts a near miss
choices.why: The mocked `expect_failures` runs catch that.

choices.text: A file out of the canonical layout
choices.why: `fmt -check` catches that.
